localChanges: A new Enhanced rule, off to start with, makes research cost half as much in the Ancient Age, rising with each age to three times in the Space Age, instead of doubling at 1 AD, so research stays dear after rushing ahead, even for the advances you skipped. With it on, research also costs more once your civilization reaches the Renaissance if the leading civilization is ahead of schedule, rather than for everyone from 1 AD (closes #1077).

log: feat: the tiles a city may work, within a number of rings by the world's own steps (#1)
feat: on the hexagonal grid, a city works the 2 rings round it (#32)

The rate of research cost follows the player's age, from 0.5 to 3, in place of doubling from AD, and catch-up applies from the player's own Renaissance. Works with either research cost and with the ages on or off; with only one of its rules on, the other half is civ1-science's. The fixed costs are rounded to whole bulbs.

The doubling from AD and the catch-up from AD become RateMultiplier and CatchUp rules, which the cost asks when given the game's rules, so a set can take the place of either; with none in force, or no rules given, the rate is v474.05's. Costs are rounded to whole bulbs.
fix: on a hexagonal grid, Civ1's distance is the fewest hex steps (#14)
